subject: Polity
description: Urban local government in India — 74th Constitutional Amendment 1992, Part IXA, three-tier municipal structure, 12th Schedule subjects, ward committees.

questions.stem: The 74TH CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT (1992) gave constitutional status to:
questions.explanation: 74TH CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT ACT (1992) — gave CONSTITUTIONAL STATUS to URBAN LOCAL BODIES (Municipalities). Came into effect 1 JUNE 1993. ADDED PART IXA + 12TH SCHEDULE + Articles 243P to 243ZG. PARALLEL: 73RD AMENDMENT (also 1992) — for PANCHAYATI RAJ (rural local govt); Part IX + 11th Schedule. THREE-TIER MUNICIPAL STRUCTURE under 74th: (1) NAGAR PANCHAYAT (for AREAS in TRANSITION from rural to urban — population threshold variable). (2) MUNICIPAL COUNCIL (for SMALLER URBAN areas). (3) MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (for LARGER urban areas — typically million-plus cities; e.g., Mumbai's BMC, Delhi's MCD, Chennai Corporation, Kolkata Corporation, Bengaluru BBMP, Hyderabad GHMC). KEY MANDATORY PROVISIONS: (1) ELECTIONS every 5 YEARS; reservation for SC/ST/Women (33% women, since 1992; many states 50%). (2) STATE ELECTION COMMISSION (SEC) conducts elections. (3) STATE FINANCE COMMISSION (every 5 years) recommends financial devolution. (4) WARD COMMITTEES in larger cities. (5) DISTRICT PLANNING COMMITTEE + METROPOLITAN PLANNING COMMITTEE for area-wise plans. (6) 18 SUBJECTS in 12th Schedule (urban planning, water, sanitation, public health, etc.). PROBLEMS: states can VARY IMPLEMENTATION; municipal finances weak; mayors often ceremonial (executive power with State-appointed Commissioner). UPSC angle: 73RD-74TH amendments core GS-2 topic; LOCAL GOVT, decentralization. PYQ FREQUENCY: 74th Amendment in UPSC, MPSC, state PSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: Which is the LARGEST type of urban local body for major cities like Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru?
questions.explanation: MUNICIPAL CORPORATION — LARGEST TYPE of urban local body, for cities with population typically > 10 lakh (1 million). Notable examples: (1) BRIHANMUMBAI MUNICIPAL CORPORATION (BMC) — Mumbai; biggest municipal budget in Asia (~₹50,000 crore/year); founded 1888. (2) MUNICIPAL CORPORATION OF DELHI (MCD) — unified back in 2022 (after 2012 trifurcation). (3) BBMP (Bruhat Bengaluru Mahanagara Palike) — Bengaluru. (4) GHMC (Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation). (5) KMC (Kolkata Municipal Corporation) — founded 1876, oldest. (6) Chennai Municipal Corp — founded 1688 (oldest in India, established by Madras Province council). (7) PCMC (Pimpri Chinchwad Municipal Corp), AMC (Ahmedabad MC), SMC (Surat MC). KEY OFFICIALS: (1) MAYOR — political head; ceremonial in most cases. (2) MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER — IAS officer; executive head; APPOINTED by state govt. (3) DEPUTY MAYOR. (4) STANDING COMMITTEE (executive body). (5) WARD COMMITTEES. (6) ELECTED COUNCILLORS — represent wards. KEY POWERS of CORPORATION: water supply, sewage + sanitation, solid-waste management, public health, building permissions, property tax collection, parks, primary education, primary health centres. CHALLENGES: revenue dependency on state grants; political tussles between Mayor + state govt + Commissioner; population pressure. UPSC angle: URBAN GOVERNANCE + smart cities mission + AMRUT scheme. PYQ FREQUENCY: municipal corporation structure in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: How many SUBJECTS are listed in the 12TH SCHEDULE (functions of municipalities)?
questions.explanation: 12TH SCHEDULE — added by 74th Amendment 1992; lists 18 SUBJECTS that may be entrusted to MUNICIPALITIES by state legislatures. KEY SUBJECTS (memorize categories — UPSC PT favorite): (1) URBAN PLANNING + town planning. (2) Regulation of land-use + building. (3) Planning for economic + social development. (4) Roads + bridges. (5) WATER SUPPLY (domestic, industrial, commercial). (6) Public health, sanitation, conservancy + solid waste management. (7) Fire services. (8) Urban forestry, ecology, environment. (9) Safeguarding interests of WEAKER SECTIONS (SCs, STs, PHs). (10) SLUM IMPROVEMENT + upgradation. (11) URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION. (12) PARKS, gardens, playgrounds. (13) PROMOTION of cultural, educational, aesthetic aspects. (14) BURIAL + cremation grounds. (15) CATTLE pounds + prevention of cruelty to animals. (16) Vital statistics — registration of BIRTHS + DEATHS. (17) Public amenities — STREET LIGHTING, parking, bus stops. (18) Regulation of SLAUGHTER HOUSES + tanneries. CONTRAST WITH 11TH SCHEDULE (PANCHAYATS, 73rd Amendment): 29 subjects — includes agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries, social forestry, drinking water, fuel + fodder, roads, rural electrification, etc. KEY DIFFERENCE: 12th Schedule subjects are 18 + URBAN focused; 11th Schedule subjects are 29 + RURAL focused. UPSC angle: comparison of 11th + 12th Schedules in GS-2; MAINS questions on local govt empowerment. PYQ FREQUENCY: 12th vs 11th Schedule numbers in UPSC PT, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Reservation for WOMEN in municipal bodies under 74th Amendment is:
questions.explanation: Article 243T (74th Amendment): not less than 1/3 of TOTAL SEATS in municipalities reserved for WOMEN, including SC/ST women (1/3 within each reservation category). Many state laws have INCREASED women's reservation to 50% — including: BIHAR (2007 — first), KARNATAKA, JHARKHAND, KERALA, MAHARASHTRA, RAJASTHAN, GUJARAT, ANDHRA PRADESH, UTTARAKHAND, ODISHA, TAMIL NADU, MADHYA PRADESH, HIMACHAL PRADESH, CHATTISGARH. RESERVATION FOR SC/ST: in proportion to their POPULATION in the area; rotated by seats. RESERVATION FOR OBC: state-by-state (e.g., Maharashtra, Karnataka have 27%; not constitutional mandatory). KEY REASONS: women's representation historically poor; reservation aimed at empowerment + decision-making access. IMPACT — STUDIES: women panchayat/municipal leaders prioritize: WATER (drinking water, public taps), SANITATION (toilets, drainage), CHILD welfare, education, ANGANWADIs. NATIONAL TRAJECTORY: women MPs/MLAs ~14-15% (low); 73rd-74th have created ~14 lakh women representatives at PRI/ULB level — the LARGEST cohort of elected women globally. NARI SHAKTI VANDAN ADHINIYAM (106TH AMENDMENT) — Sept 2023 — passed by Parliament: 33% reservation for WOMEN in LOK SABHA + STATE LEGISLATURES; effective POST-DELIMITATION (Census-based, expected 2027-29). UPSC angle: gender + governance + women's empowerment, GS-2 + GS-1 social issues. PYQ FREQUENCY: women's reservation in UPSC, MPSC 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: WHO conducts MUNICIPAL ELECTIONS in a state?
questions.explanation: STATE ELECTION COMMISSION (SEC) — conducts municipal + panchayat elections; created under 74th + 73rd Amendments (Articles 243K, 243ZA). NOT to be confused with ELECTION COMMISSION OF INDIA (ECI) — which conducts only PARLIAMENTARY + STATE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY + STATE LEGISLATIVE COUNCIL + Office of PRESIDENT/VP elections. KEY POWERS of SEC: (1) Superintendence, direction, conduct of all local body elections. (2) Preparation of voter rolls. (3) Demarcation of constituencies. (4) Election dispute resolution. (5) Each state has its own SEC; some UTs share with neighboring states. STATE ELECTION COMMISSIONER: appointed by GOVERNOR; tenure 5 years (or as state law); REMOVAL only in same manner as HIGH COURT JUDGE (i.e., difficult — to ensure independence). KEY: SECs have STATE-LEVEL constitutional protection. INDIA's MULTI-LEVEL elections oversight: (1) ECI (Centre) — Lok Sabha + Vidhan Sabha elections. (2) SEC (State) — Panchayat + Municipal elections. CHALLENGES: (1) State govts SOMETIMES delay/postpone local elections through legislation or administrative decisions. (2) SC has held — 5-year-cycle is MANDATORY; cannot extend without due reason. UPSC ANGLE: ELECTION COMMISSIONS + DEMOCRACY HEALTH; recent issues like delayed local elections in some states (e.g., Karnataka BBMP elections delayed several years). PYQ FREQUENCY: ECI vs SEC distinction in UPSC, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: Under 74th Amendment, the TENURE of a Municipality is:
questions.explanation: Article 243U (74th Amendment): MUNICIPALITY's TENURE is 5 YEARS from date of FIRST MEETING after election. After dissolution: ELECTIONS within 6 MONTHS. ELECTION CONSTITUTION must finish: (a) Before expiry of 5-year term, OR (b) Within 6 months from dissolution. KEY: NO POSTPONEMENT beyond 5 years allowed unless: (a) Pre-existing emergency under Article 356 (President's Rule). (b) ELECTORAL ROLLS not ready — narrow ground. SC RULINGS (Kishan Singh Tomar 2006, etc.): 5-year cycle is MANDATORY; SECs MUST hold timely elections; mere delay in delimitation/reservation cannot be excuse. RECENT CASES (2022-2024): (1) KARNATAKA — BBMP (Bengaluru) elections delayed since 2020 (5 years overdue as of 2025) — controversial; SC asked govt to act. (2) HIMACHAL PRADESH, KERALA — local-body elections held on time. (3) WEST BENGAL — held panchayat elections 2023, with controversy over violence. KEY: when local body is dissolved (e.g., due to political reasons), ELECTED BODY must be re-installed within 6 MONTHS — IF less than 6 months left in original term, no fresh election required (acceptable to leave seat vacant briefly). DISSOLUTION GROUNDS: defeat in vote of confidence, mass resignation, dissolution by state govt (with reasons). UPSC ANGLE: democratic decentralization, SC's role in protecting local govt. PYQ FREQUENCY: tenure rules in UPSC PT, MPSC 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: WHICH committee ('Father of urban local self-government in India') recommended structure now reflected in 74th Amendment?

options.option_text: Rao Committee on URBAN local govt (1987)

questions.explanation: RAO COMMITTEE ('Committee on Urban Local Bodies' headed by KN RAO, 1987) — recommended major reforms in URBAN local government, leading to 74th Amendment (1992). RECOMMENDATIONS included: 5-year fixed tenure, women's reservation, financial devolution, ward committees, etc. EARLIER URBAN-FOCUSED REFORMS: ZAKARIA COMMITTEE (1963), RURAL-URBAN RELATIONS COMMITTEE (1966). KEY URBAN SCHEMES + COMMITTEES (memorize): (1) URBAN PLANNING in 5-Year Plans (1st onwards). (2) JNNURM (Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission) 2005 — under PM Manmohan Singh; massive urban infrastructure programme. (3) AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation + Urban Transformation) 2015 — successor to JNNURM. (4) SMART CITIES MISSION 2015 — 100 cities; tech + urban planning + sustainability. (5) HRIDAY (Heritage Cities) 2015. (6) PMAY-U (Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana — Urban) — affordable housing. (7) SWACHH BHARAT MISSION-Urban — sanitation, ODF cities. CONTRAST WITH RURAL: BALWANT RAI MEHTA Committee (1957) — recommended 3-tier PANCHAYATI RAJ; states implemented 1959 onwards (Rajasthan first, 2 Oct 1959). ASHOK MEHTA Committee (1977) — recommended 2-tier (district + Mandal) instead of 3-tier; not adopted. P.K. THUNGON Committee (1988) — recommended PRI constitutional status + 5-year term. L.M. SINGHVI Committee (1986) — also recommended PRI reforms. UPSC angle: history of decentralization in India. PYQ FREQUENCY: Rao Committee + 74th Amendment in UPSC, MPSC 1× per 2 cycles.
